x: Plasma is the transport medium, RBCs carry O₂ on haemoglobin, WBCs defend the body and platelets clot blood, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the function of each blood component.

x: Option C is incorrect: Rh incompatibility matters in both pregnancy and transfusion. Rh+ means the RhD antigen is present and Rh− means it is absent.
t: Check each statement for "but not".

x: Both are true and R explains A: an Rh− mother can make antibodies against an Rh+ baby's red cells, endangering later pregnancies.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All three are correct: group A has A antigen and anti-B, AB has both antigens and no antibodies, and O has no antigens and both antibodies.
t: Recall that plasma has antibodies against the antigens it lacks.
s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Blood group A has A antigen on RBCs and Anti-B antibody in plasma.
II. Blood group AB has A and B antigens and no plasma antibodies.
III. Blood group O has no RBC antigens and has Anti-A and Anti-B antibodies in plasma.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Karl Landsteiner and Alexander Wiener discovered the Rh factor through work with rhesus monkey blood. Landsteiner had earlier discovered the ABO blood groups in 1900.
t: Recall the discoverers of blood groups.
s: Who discovered the Rh factor in blood?

x: All four are carried by plasma: proteins, hormones, antibodies and clotting factors.
t: Recall what plasma carries.

x: All three are correct: RBCs are erythrocytes, WBCs leucocytes and platelets thrombocytes.
t: Recall the other names of blood cells.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. RBCs are also called erythrocytes.
II. WBCs are also called leucocytes.
III. Platelets are also called thrombocytes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: haemoglobin is the oxygen-carrying respiratory pigment, and fibrinogen becomes fibrin in a clot.
t: Recall the roles of blood proteins.

x: Albumin maintains blood's osmotic pressure, globulins include the antibodies, fibrinogen becomes fibrin in a clot, and haemoglobin is the oxygen-carrying pigment. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Link each blood protein to its role.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Albumin
(b) Globulins
(c) Fibrinogen
(d) Haemoglobin

List-II
(i) Maintains the osmotic pressure of blood
(ii) Include the antibodies (gamma globulins)
(iii) Converted to fibrin during clotting
(iv) Respiratory pigment that carries oxygen

x: Both are true: erythroblastosis fetalis, a haemolytic disease of the newborn, results from Rh incompatibility.
t: Recall the disease from Rh incompatibility.

x: Thrombin converts fibrinogen into fibrin threads that trap blood cells into a clot. Prothrombin is its inactive precursor and heparin an anticoagulant.
t: Recall the clotting cascade.

x: Option B is incorrect: leukopenia is a fall in WBCs; a rise is leukocytosis. Anaemia, thrombocytopenia and polycythaemia are described rightly.
t: Discriminate -penia (decrease) from -cytosis (increase).

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: alum's clot-promoting action is the opposite effect and says nothing about how heparin prevents clotting.
t: Check whether R is a cause or an opposite fact.

x: Anaemia is low RBCs or haemoglobin, polycythaemia high RBC volume, haemophilia an inherited clotting disorder and thrombocytopenia low platelets, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the blood disorders.

x: I, II and III are correct: platelets start clotting, prothrombin is a clotting factor and fibrin forms the mesh. IV is false because heparin prevents clotting.
t: Discriminate coagulants from anticoagulants.

x: Vitamin K is needed by the liver to make clotting factors such as prothrombin; deficiency causes bleeding.
t: Recall the role of vitamin K.

x: All three are correct: leukaemia is a cancer of white cells starting in bone marrow, and erythroblastosis fetalis comes from Rh incompatibility.
t: Recall the blood disorders.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: coronary arteries bring blood to the heart muscle, while cardiac veins drain it; one does not explain the other.
t: Check whether R is a cause or a paired fact.

x: The tricuspid valve guards RA to RV, the mitral LA to LV, the pulmonary valve RV to pulmonary artery and the aortic valve LV to aorta, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the four heart valves.

x: I and II are correct: the aorta carries blood from the left ventricle to the body, and the venae cavae return it to the right atrium. III is false because pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.
t: Recall the exception: pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The aorta carries blood from the left ventricle to the body.
II. The vena cava carries blood from the body to the right atrium.
III. The pulmonary vein carries deoxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: The right atrium receives the venae cavae, the right ventricle the right atrium, the left atrium the pulmonary veins and the left ventricle the left atrium, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
t: Recall the path of blood through the heart.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the blood's low oxygen is its state, not why the pulmonary artery carries it from the right ventricle to the lungs.
t: Check whether R explains the route or only the content.

x: The SA node in the right atrium fires the impulses that set the heartbeat, making it the natural pacemaker. The AV node relays them.
t: Discriminate the SA node (pacemaker) from the AV node (relay).

x: Option B is incorrect: urea is made in the liver by the ornithine cycle; the kidney only filters it out. The kidneys also balance ions and pH.
t: Discriminate where urea is made from where it is removed.

x: Both are true and R explains A: blood passes through the heart twice per round, once for the lungs and once for the body, hence "double" circulation.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The kidney filters blood and forms urine, regulates long-term blood pressure, urea is made in the liver and urine flows kidney → ureter → bladder → urethra, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
t: Recall the facts about the kidney.

x: All three are correct: in diastole the chambers relax and fill, in systole the ventricles pump, and urine output averages about 1.5 litres a day.
t: Recall the cardiac cycle and urine output.

x: The impulse runs SA node → AV node → conduction system, the resting rate is about 72–75 per minute, and tachycardia is above 100, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-i.
t: Recall heart rate and conduction.

x: Christiaan Barnard did the first heart transplant, Robert Jarvik made the Jarvik-7, Barney Clark was its first recipient and William Harvey found circulation, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the heart firsts.

x: Both are true: urea is the main nitrogenous waste removed by the kidneys, and they keep extracellular fluid volume steady.
t: Recall the functions of the kidney.

x: I and II are correct: the kidneys remove wastes and toxins, and normal urine is slightly acidic, about pH 6.0. III is false because urea is formed in the liver and only filtered out by the kidneys.
t: Recall where urea is made and urine's pH.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The kidneys remove metabolic wastes and toxins.
II. The pH of urine is approximately 6.0.
III. Urea is formed in the kidneys.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: The nephron is the kidney's structural and functional unit; each kidney has about a million. Dialysis is the artificial filter.
t: Recall the unit of the kidney.

x: Both are true and R explains A: without ADH the kidneys cannot reabsorb water, so large amounts of dilute urine are passed.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The glomerulus filters blood, Bowman's capsule receives the filtrate, the loop of Henle concentrates it and the collecting duct finishes concentrating urine, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the role of each part of the nephron.

x: All three are correct: aquatic animals excrete ammonia, mammals including humans urea, and birds, reptiles and insects uric acid.
t: Recall the nitrogenous waste of each animal group.
s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Ammonia is associated with ammonotelic organisms.
II. Urea is associated with ureotelic organisms, including humans.
III. Uric acid is associated with uricotelic birds, reptiles and insects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Option C is incorrect: kidney damage harms both filtration and excretion. Calcium oxalate stones, dialysis and renal failure are described rightly.
t: Check each statement for "but not".

x: The proximal tubule does most selective reabsorption, the distal tubule fine-tunes by reabsorption and secretion, the loop of Henle concentrates the filtrate and the collecting duct gives final concentration. The answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Discriminate proximal from distal tubule.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Proximal convoluted tubule
 b. Distal convoluted tubule
 c. Loop of Henle
 d. Collecting duct

List-II
 i. Regulation, reabsorption and secretion
 ii. Major selective reabsorption
 iii. Concentration and osmoregulation
 iv. Final urine concentration

x: The renal artery brings blood to the kidney for filtering. The renal vein returns filtered blood, and reabsorption happens in the tubules.
t: Discriminate renal artery from renal vein.
